commentary: Current spot rates show GPU rental prices rising or holding firm across all generations—H100 up 40% since Oct 2025 to ~$2.85-$3.15/hr median, B200 at $5.50-$5.80/hr vs sub-$5 in Jan 2026—contradicting depreciation narratives and signaling persistent demand. The divergence in hyperscaler depreciation policy (Amazon shortening to 5 years while Meta/MSFT/GOOGL/ORCL extend to 5.5-6 years on identical hardware) creates a $176B-$228B cumulative GAAP earnings tailwind through 2028 that may reverse if utilization or resale values disappoint. CoreWeave's CDS blowout to 855 bps despite investment-grade GPU debt ratings highlights refinancing risk in a $21B+ debt stack collateralized by rapidly depreciating chips, yet rising on-demand rates and tightening Blackwell supply suggest the waterfall remains steep enough to support both debt service and current rental economics—at least through mid-2027.
